newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end lower but Greenspan lifts gloom.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end lower but Greenspan lifts gloom.

text.p: Dutch shares ended slightly easier on Tuesday but the market was cheered late in the day by upbeat remarks on the U.S. economy by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, who was testifying to a Senate committee.
The AEX index of leading shares closed just 1.31 points lower at 672.32, well above the day's low at 665.66 points.

The market came under pressure early on from a weaker bond market and amid fears of a potential equity shake-out similar to the one which followed Greenspan's comments last month when he described world share markets as overheated.

But Greenspan this time painted an encouraging picture of the U.S. economy, although warned of the risks of wage-driven inflation. He described the rise on Wall Street as breathtaking and said the economy grew around three percent in 1996.
"The comments were well received by the financial markets and there was a feeling of relief that the sell-off we saw last time wasn't going to happen again," one dealer commented.
Greenspan's testimony pulled Dutch shares off their lows, but financial issues remained under pressure and closed mixed.
Banking group ING ended 0.40 guilders up at 70.00 but ABN AMRO lost 0.70 to close at 118.80 guilders.

Brewing giant Heineken had a bad day, amid market speculation of a negative report on the European beer market. The rumours, not substantiated, but were enough to dent the share price, which closed down 8.00 guilders at 289.20.
However, this too climbed off its earlier low of 285.60.
Other index heavywights closed little changed. Publisher Elsevier was up 0.10 at 28.10 and Philips unchanged at 76.30.
Elsewhere, photocopier maker Oce van der Grinten broke above phsychological chart resistance at 200 guilders reflecting analysts' repeated buy recommendations. It closed up 5.80 at 204.50 guilders.
